- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +3–5% above peak.
- If official supply net is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside; add 1–3% downward adjustment.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often fails to capture immediate drop; apply early correction at 10–15 day horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 1.00 followed by 0.00), model overreacts; reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive bearish sentiment days.
- In high-event periods (≥18 events/30d), model tends to overfit recent highs; use 3-day moving average of true prices to anchor forecast baseline.
